;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[November 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Three [[Afghan National Police|policemen]] are killed and two others are injured after a bomb on a motorbike explodes near a [[police checkpoint]] in [[Herat]], [[Herat Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-167453 (TOLOnews)]
***At least four people are killed and another eight injured after a [[mortar (weapon)|mortar]] shell hit the governor of [[Kunduz]]'s compound, as soldiers were playing volleyball. [https://tolonews.com/index.php/afghanistan-167473 (TOLOnews)]
*Thirty-two civilians are killed during an attack by an armed group against the [[Amhara people|Amhara]] [[ethnic group]] in [[Welega Province]], [[Ethiopia]]. It is suspected that at least twenty other people have been killed in the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/2/horrendous-attack-leave-dozens-killed-in-western-ethiopia (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*The city of [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]], sets its [[minimum wage]] to [[Swiss franc|CHF]]23 ([[United States dollar|US$]]25) per hour per the results of a September [[referendum]], becoming the highest in the world. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54745033 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Aegean Sea earthquake]]
**Forty-five more people are found dead under debris in [[İzmir]] after an [[earthquake]] struck [[Greece]] and [[Turkey]] two days ago, bringing the death toll to 85. More than 1,000 people are injured. [https://www.reuters.com/article/BigStory12/idUSKBN27I0AP (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 434 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide death toll to 35,298, a day after announcing stringent new restrictions including the closure of schools, universities and mosques in most of the country. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20201101-irans-daily-covid-death-toll-hits-record-high/ (Middle East Monitor)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Israel]] begins testing its vaccine on humans. In the first trial, 80 volunteers will take part, and will be expanded to 960 people in December. If the two trials are successful, the third stage of the trial will occur with 30,000 volunteers in April or May. If these stages are successful, the vaccine could be ready for the general public by the end of summer 2021. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/volunteer-to-receive-1st-israeli-vaccine-shot-hails-historic-opportunity/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 972 new recoveries in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total of recoveries to 22,220. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2020/11/01/covid-19-malaysia-records-972-recoveries-outstrips-new-cases-at-952/1918349 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] announces that from November 7, it will expand its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mandatory mask policy]] to department stores, theme parks, spas, wedding halls and other places as part of new [[social distancing]] rules aimed at preparing for a prolonged outbreak. It also introduces a new five-tiered social distancing system, which replaces a three-level system that was designed to mitigate the economic impact of the pandemic. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20201101001054320 (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Jean Castex]] announces in a televised interview on [[TF1]] that the [[Government of France|government]] would introduce a ban on the sale of all 'non-essential' items in supermarkets from November 3 as part of a lockdown measure to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20201101-french-pm-announces-ban-on-sale-of-non-essential-items-in-supermarkets-from-tuesday (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 18,665 new infections in the last 24 hours, a single day record, taking the nationwide total to 1,636,781. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-russia-cases/russias-new-coronavirus-cases-hit-record-high-of-18665-idUKKBN27H14S (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]], [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns]]
****Starting tomorrow, [[Geneva]] will impose a partial lockdown until November 29, after it reported more than 1,000 new cases in the past several days. According to new rules, restaurants, bars, and non-essential shops will be closed at 7:00 p.m. local time. In addition, cinemas, museums, concert halls, gyms, swimming pools and ice rinks will also be closed. However, schools will remain open. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/geneva-introduces-partial-lockdown/46134304 (Swiss Info)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Australia]] records no new cases of COVID-19 for the first time since June 9, according to Health Minister [[Greg Hunt]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-54768038 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[France–Turkey relations]]
**Amid deteriorating relations between the two countries, [[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] accuses [[Turkey]] of adopting a "bellicose stance towards its [[NATO]] allies", and that it was essential that the "[[Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] respects France, respects the [[European Union]], respects its values, does not tell lies and does not utter insults". He also says Turkey's [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war|military intervention]] in [[Syria]] was "a surprise and aggression for NATO allies", and that Turkey has "not respected" an [[arms embargo]] on [[Libya]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/01/macron-criticises-turkeys-imperial-inclinations-as-row-between-countries-escalates (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Foreign relations of the Cook Islands]]
**The [[Prime Minister of the Cook Islands|Prime Minister]] of the [[Cook Islands]], [[Mark Brown (Cook Islands)|Mark Brown]], calls the threat of five nations ([[Palau]], [[Nauru]], [[Kiribati]], the [[Marshall Islands]] and the [[Federated States of Micronesia]]) withdrawing from the [[Pacific Islands Forum]] in case their nominee is not elected as Secretary-General as "premature" and "extreme". [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/429636/cook-islands-pm-describes-forum-withdrawal-threat-as-extreme (RNZ)]

;Law and crime
*Hong Kong [[pro-democracy]] lawmakers [[Eddie Chu]], [[Raymond Chan Chi-chuen]], [[Wu Chi-wai]], [[Andrew Wan]], [[Helena Wong (politician)|Helena Wong]], [[Fernando Cheung]] and [[Kwok Wing-kin]] are arrested for "scuffles with [[pro-Beijing]] legislators" last May. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-54768209 (BBC News)]
*The main [[defendant]] in the trial of the [[Charlie Hebdo shooting|mass shooting in January 2015]] at the ''[[Charlie Hebdo]]'' [[headquarters]] tests positive for COVID-19. The other defendants will be tested, prompting the judge to suspend court for several days. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54768212 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections 
*[[2020 Algerian constitutional referendum]]
**Citizens of [[Algeria]] head to the polls to decide over a proposed amendmend of the country's [[Constitution of Algeria|constitution]]. The proposal is supported by [[President of Algeria|president]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] and the [[Military of Algeria|military]] as a reaction to widespread [[2019–20 Algerian protests|protests]] which resulted in the resignation of long-term president [[Abdelaziz Bouteflika]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/algeria-votes-in-constitutional-referendum-after-pro-democracy-protests/a-55462803 (DW)]
*[[2020 Moldovan presidential election]]
**[[Moldovans]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Moldova|President]]. Incumbent [[Igor Dodon]] seeks a second term against main opposition candidate and former [[Prime Minister of Moldova|Prime Minister]] [[Maia Sandu]], who wants closer [[Moldova–European Union relations|ties with the]] [[European Union]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-moldova-election/moldovans-vote-in-presidential-election-as-pro-moscow-incumbent-bids-for-second-term-idUSKBN27H11L (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Georgian parliamentary election]]
**Preliminary results see [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]'s ruling party [[Georgian Dream]] winning the country's latest parliamentary election. The announcement sparks protests throughout the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/1/georgia-ruling-party-declares-victory (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kashmir conflict]]
**[[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Pakistani Prime Minister]] [[Imran Khan]] announces that [[Gilgit-Baltistan]] has been granted "provisional provincial status" to mark the territory's independence day. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/pak-pm-imran-khan-gives-provisional-provincial-status-to-gilgit-baltistan/story-O5mtkrQDQLh1VtSgF2yoaJ.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/pakistan/pakistan-prime-minister-imran-khan-grants-provisional-provincial-status-to-gilgit-baltistan-1.1604218999490 (''Gulf News'')]
